items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5615

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the public service law and the general business law,
in relation to providing for unlisted telephone numbers without charge
for certain victims of domestic violence


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
This bill would provide for unlisted telephone numbers without charge
for victims of domestic violence for whose benefit an order of
protection has been issued.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill would amend Section 91 of the Public Service Law
to provide to victims of domestic violence for whose benefit a
permanent order of protection has been issued, for the duration of
such order, an unlisted telephone number or a modified or alternative
listing free of any charge otherwise applicable.

Section 2 of the bill would amend the general business law by adding a
new section 399-zz, which would require cable telephone providers to
provide to victims of domestic violence for whose benefit a permanent
order of protection has been issued, for the duration of such order,
an unlisted telephone number or a modified or alternative listing free
of any charge otherwise applicable.

Section 3 of the bill would require the Offices for prevention of
domestic violence and children and family services to assist the
Public Service Commission.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The State has the inherent authority under the doctrine of Parens
patriae to protect children and citizens of limited capacity, and
standing to bring suit on behalf of its quasi-sovereign interests,
such as "health, comfort, and welfare" of the people.  ( SEE, GIBBS V.
TITELMAN , 369 F. Supp. 38, 54 (1973). Similarly, the State has the
moral obligation and authority, and the ability to act, to protect the
health, safety and welfare of the people, and particularly so, as
here, where victims of domestic violence are seeking the State's aid
to obtain refuge and protection from their aggressor.

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the
National Institute of Justice, 25% of women have experience domestic
violence in their lifetime. ( SEE, EXTENT, NATURE AND CONSEQUENCES OF
INTIMATE PARTNER VIOLENCE , July 2000.) Estimates range from 960,000
incidents of violence against a current or former spouse, boyfriend or
girlfriend, to as many as 1.3 million women who are physically abused
by an intimate partner each year. (See, U.S.  Department of Justice,
 VIOLENCE BY INTIMATES:  ANALYSIS OF DATA ON CRIMES BY CURRENT OR
FORMER SPOUSES, BOYFRIENDS AND GIRLFRIENDS , March 1998.) Nearly 81%
of women stalked by a current or former intimate partner are also
physically assaulted by that person, and roughly 31% are also sexually
assaulted by that person. (See, Patricia Tjaden & Nancy Thoennes,
"Stalking in America," National Institute for Justice (1998)).
Finally, the estimated cost of intimate partner violence exceeds $5.8
billion each year, more than 70% of which is for direct medical and
mental health services. (See, "Costs of intimate partner Violence
Against Women in the United States," 2003, Centers for Disease Control
and Prevention.)

It is time for New York State's victims of domestic violence to be
able obtain an unlisted or modified telephone number so their
aggressors would not be able to circumvent the permanent order of
protection barring them from harassing, intimidating and sometimes
coercing the victim over the telephone.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
Although this is a new bill, a similar bill has the following
legislative history over the past nine years.

S.1518 (2008) - Energy and Telecommunications
A.2934 (2008) - Passed Assembly
S.1553 (2006) - Energy and Telecommunications
A.9275 (2006) - Corporations, Authorities and Commissions
S.3279 (2004) - Energy and Telecommunications
A.3772 (2004) - Passed Assembly
S.6427 (2002) - Energy and Telecommunications
A.1669 (2002) - Passed Assembly
A.3254B (2000) - Rules

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE A
This act shall take effect one hundred twenty days after it shall have
become law.
